B8-02-sigmoid-growth-curve-graph

Line graph with "time" on the horizontal axis and "size (height or dry mass)" on the vertical axis, showing a smooth S-shaped (sigmoid) curve in soft green. Divide the curve with light vertical dashed lines into four regions and label them below the axis: lag phase, log (exponential) phase, deceleration phase, stationary phase. Add a small text arrow pointing to the steepest part. Axis labels: time, size.
B8-03-human-vs-insect-growth

Two small line graphs side by side, both with "time" on the horizontal axis and "length" on the vertical axis. Left: human growth curve from birth to 20 years, rising steeply in infancy, then steadily through childhood, with a second steep rise at puberty, then levelling off; label "infancy growth", "adolescent growth spurt", "adult size". Right: a staircase-shaped curve for an insect, with flat steps and sudden rises; label each sudden rise "moult (ecdysis)" and the flat parts "no increase in length (hard exoskeleton)". Titles: human growth curve, insect (stepwise) growth curve. Soft blue and green lines.
B8-01-root-tip-zones-section

Longitudinal section of a root tip, drawn vertically with the tip at the bottom. Show the root cap at the very tip, then above it a short region of small, tightly packed dividing cells (some with visible chromosomes), then a region of long, stretched cells with large vacuoles, then a region where cells are specialised, with root hairs growing out of the epidermis and long xylem vessels in the centre. Use brackets on the side to mark the zones. Soft green and cream colours.
B8-05-bean-seed-anatomy

Three views of a bean seed side by side. 1. External view of a whole kidney-shaped bean seed from the side showing the smooth testa, the oval hilum on the inner curve and the tiny micropyle next to it. 2. The same seed with the testa removed and the two cotyledons opened apart like a book, showing the embryo axis lying along one cotyledon with the curved radicle and the small plumule with two tiny folded leaves. 3. A simple diagram of the embryo axis alone showing radicle, hypocotyl, point of attachment of cotyledons, epicotyl and plumule. Soft beige seed coat, pale yellow-green cotyledons, light green embryo.
B8-07-seed-germination-conditions-experiment

Four test tubes in a rack, labelled A, B, C and D, each containing a few bean seeds. Tube A: moist cotton wool at the bottom, seeds with short white radicles and green shoots, open top; tag "water + air + warmth (control)". Tube B: dry cotton wool, dry unchanged seeds; tag "no water". Tube C: seeds at the bottom covered by boiled and cooled water with a thin yellow layer of oil on top, unchanged seeds; tag "no oxygen". Tube D: moist cotton wool with unchanged seeds, shown inside an outline of a refrigerator with a snowflake symbol; tag "cold (about 4 °C)". Soft blue water, yellow oil, beige seeds, green shoots.
B8-08-germination-oxygen-requirement-apparatus

Two identical sealed conical flasks side by side, each closed with a rubber stopper, each holding a small wire gauze platform or a hanging muslin bag with moist cotton wool and bean seeds above a liquid at the bottom. Left flask: brown liquid at the bottom, seeds unchanged. Right flask: clear liquid, seeds germinating with short white radicles. Soft colours.
B8-09-epigeal-germination-stages

A sequence of five stages of epigeal germination of a bean seed, drawn left to right with a brown soil line across the middle. Stage 1: a swollen bean seed below the soil line with the radicle just emerging. Stage 2: the radicle growing downwards with some root hairs, and the hypocotyl forming an arch that is just pushing up through the soil surface. Stage 3: the hypocotyl arch above ground, pulling up the two cotyledons with the testa still partly attached. Stage 4: the hypocotyl straightened, the two cotyledons opened and green above ground, the plumule with two small leaves between them, lateral roots below. Stage 5: a young seedling with expanded first foliage leaves, shrivelled cotyledons and a branched root system. Soft brown soil, green shoots, beige seed.
B8-10-hypogeal-maize-germination-stages

A sequence of four stages of germination of a maize grain, drawn left to right with a brown soil line across the middle. Stage 1: a swollen maize grain below the soil line with the coleorhiza and radicle emerging downward. Stage 2: the radicle longer with root hairs and a few seminal roots, and a pointed coleoptile growing straight upward toward the soil surface. Stage 3: the coleoptile breaking through the soil surface and the first green leaf emerging from its tip. Stage 4: a young maize seedling with two or three long narrow leaves, the grain still buried below the soil and shrivelling, a fibrous root system with seminal roots and adventitious roots from the stem base. Soft brown soil, yellow grain, green leaves.
B8-11-epigeal-hypogeal-comparison

Two seedlings side by side for comparison, with a brown soil line across both. Left: a young bean seedling (epigeal) with two green cotyledons above the soil, a long hypocotyl between the soil surface and the cotyledons, a short epicotyl above them and the first foliage leaves. Right: a young broad bean or pea seedling (hypogeal) with the seed and its two cotyledons still below the soil, a short hypocotyl, and a long epicotyl rising from below ground up through the soil to the first foliage leaves. Labels on both: cotyledons, hypocotyl, epicotyl, plumule leaves, soil level, root. Titles: epigeal germination (bean, cowpea), hypogeal germination (broad bean, pea). Soft brown, green and beige colours.
B8-12-seed-food-mobilisation-flowchart

Flow diagram of food mobilisation in a germinating maize grain, drawn as a longitudinal section of the grain with arrows. Show the embryo with an arrow going to the aleurone layer; from the aleurone layer arrows and "protease" going into the endosperm; inside the endosperm show "starch → maltose → glucose" and "protein → amino acids"; then arrows carrying sugars and amino acids from the endosperm across the scutellum into the growing plumule and radicle. Soft yellow endosperm, light green embryo, blue arrows.
B8-04-seed-germination-mass-change

Line graph with "days after sowing" on the horizontal axis (0 to 20) and "mass" on the vertical axis. Two curves: a blue curve for fresh mass rising steadily from day 0; and a green curve for dry mass that falls slightly from day 0 to a low point at about day 7, then rises steadily after. Add a small marker at the low point.
B8-06-maize-grain-anatomy

Two views of a maize grain side by side. 1. External view of a whole maize grain (flattened, wedge-shaped, yellow) showing the paler oval embryo area on one face, the silk scar at the top and the point of attachment at the narrow base. 2. Longitudinal section through the embryo region showing the thin pericarp fused with testa around the outside, the thin aleurone layer just inside it, the large endosperm filling most of the grain (horny and floury parts shown in slightly different shades of yellow), the shield-shaped scutellum pressed against the endosperm, the plumule enclosed by the coleoptile pointing upward, and the radicle enclosed by the coleorhiza pointing downward. Soft yellow and cream colours with a light green embryo.
